title: Intermittent Timeouts to an External API
intro: Your app occasionally times out calling a third-party payments API. It works most of the time, which is what makes it annoying.

steps.prompt: First, distinguish 'timeout' from 'refused' — try a direct request.
steps.fake_output:
*   Trying 203.0.113.10:443...
* Connection timed out after 5001 milliseconds
steps.hint: A timeout (not 'connection refused') usually means packets are being silently dropped somewhere, not that the port is closed.

steps.prompt: Check if DNS is returning a consistent IP each time, or flapping between multiple.
steps.hint: Multiple IPs means DNS round-robins between them — worth checking if only one is unhealthy.

steps.prompt: Test connectivity to each IP directly.
steps.fake_output:
nc: connect to 203.0.113.10 port 443 (tcp) failed: Operation timed out
Connection to 203.0.113.11 443 port [tcp/https] succeeded!
steps.hint: Test both IPs separately — DNS round-robin means roughly half your requests are silently going to the broken one.

steps.prompt: Check your own outbound firewall rules in case egress is the issue, not the remote side.
steps.fake_output:
Chain OUTPUT (policy ACCEPT)
target  prot  source        destination
DROP    tcp   0.0.0.0/0     203.0.113.10
steps.hint: Check if there's an explicit DROP rule for that specific IP — sometimes these get added and forgotten.

resolution: Two things were true at once: DNS was round-robining between two IPs for the payments API, and a stale firewall rule on your own server was dropping outbound traffic to exactly one of those IPs. Since DNS alternated per-request, roughly half your calls silently hung until timeout while the other half succeeded instantly — explaining the 'intermittent' pattern perfectly. The fix is removing the stale DROP rule; the API provider's DNS setup wasn't actually the problem, it just made the real problem look random.
